prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators, and the first experimental observation of the quantum spin Hall state in HgTe quantum wells

statement.case_for: After the full first-round exchange I keep topological insulators as my preferred single-part prize. The scientific case is a complete chain: Kane and Mele's 2005 Z2 classification and quantum spin Hall proposal, then Molenkamp's HgTe edge-channel measurement, followed by fifteen to twenty years of independent confirmation by transport, ARPES, STM and imaging in many materials. It introduced a new class of quantum matter whose protected edge and surface states changed how band structure is classified, and the interpretation has not shifted. The round-1 files strengthened rather than weakened the case: Danielsson moved to the same trio, so three members now explicitly back the Kane, Mele, Molenkamp credit, and every member who commented agrees that Kane and Mele must not be separated. Of the three serious candidates it is the most mature, and its weak point is allocation, which I judge to be a limit on the citation wording and not a reason to doubt the discovery.
statement.case_against: The credit remains the genuine weakness. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang's HgTe proposal, which made Molenkamp's experiment possible, and Fu, Moore and Balents for the three-dimensional theory cannot be represented within three names, and Hasan's 3D ARPES work is left out. Any citation will therefore describe a partial picture, and a committee that regards that as misstating the origin of the work could reasonably prefer the cleaner two-name B034. The 2016 prize on topological phases and phase transitions is a second point some members weigh more heavily than I do, and I cannot settle priority details from the supplied record alone.

responses.point: Kroll holds B034 as a clean two-name invention with a settled interpretation, independent 10^-18 reproduction, and says the 2005 comb prize and the pending redefinition of the second are the main reservations; he discloses his Boulder stay in Hall's laboratory.
responses.response: I accept that the Katori-Ye attribution is the cleanest on the shortlist and that the clocks are mature and reproduced, which is why B034 is my first alternative. Your own two reservations, the comb overlap and the unfinished redefinition, are real but not what separates us. The difference is that topological classification created a new class of matter, while the clock is an extraordinary advance in the precision of an established technique. I also agree with Lindroth and the chair that your Hall-laboratory link should be declared and weighed openly. Given that, I would not make cleanliness of credit the deciding criterion, because a tidy attribution does not substitute for the weight of the discovery.

responses.point: Danielsson moved from Kane, Molenkamp and Hasan to Kane, Mele and Molenkamp in round 1 and keeps a citation built on the Z2 topological insulator and HgTe quantum wells, while saying a Hasan-based 3D case is still conceivable.
responses.response: I welcome the move to Mele, since the Z2 invariant and the quantum spin Hall proposal are one joint result and splitting them would be hard to defend. On the chair's question about the 3D branch, I would keep the citation to the two-dimensional prediction-plus-first-realisation chain. Putting Hasan in means choosing between him and Mele, and I do not think the committee can justify dropping a co-originator of the Z2 theory to cover a branch that also rests on Fu, Kane, Mele, Moore and Balents. The 3D work is better treated as the confirming consequence than as a credited part. I would accept Hasan only if the committee decides the prize must cover the 3D branch, and that would cost a theory slot.

responses.point: Eriksson prefers B046 with MacDonald, Bistritzer and Jarillo-Herrero, but states that he could be persuaded to recognise B028 first because it is more mature and the pairing mechanism in twisted graphene is unsettled.
responses.response: That concession is the key point for this round. The prediction-then-experiment arc of the Bistritzer-MacDonald model is beautiful, and I keep B046 as an alternative, but with experiments eight years old, an open pairing mechanism, a contested Andrei or Bistritzer third slot and Cao outside the credited names, its allocation problem is sharper than for B028 and its maturity is weaker. If you accept that B028 can be defended on attribution with the Kane, Mele, Molenkamp citation, I think it is the configuration on which your first-choice and fallback positions meet, and it also meets Mehlig's stated fallback. I would ask that B046 be considered seriously for a later year.

responses.point: Mehlig prefers B046 with MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero and Andrei but describes B028 as the safer choice on timing and mature, with allocation and the 2016 prize as the cost.
responses.response: You and I agree on the facts: B028 is more mature, and its cost is allocation and the 2016 overlap. We differ on how much those costs matter. The 2016 prize honoured topological phase transitions and quantum Hall precursors, not time-reversal-protected edge states or the Z2 classification, so I treat the overlap as limited. I also do not think your Andrei third slot resolves the B046 attribution, since Bistritzer, as co-author of the continuum model, and Cao remain unrepresented. A citation that rests on the prediction and first observation avoids the mechanism question you wish to avoid for B046, but B028 does that with fifteen additional years of confirmation.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will treat the 2016 topological-phases prize as a reason to wait on B028, which Lindroth and Kroll weigh more than I do.
Whether the omitted Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang, Fu, Moore and Balents contributions can be handled by citation wording alone, or whether the committee regards the misattribution risk as disqualifying.
Whether a majority of members can be found for any one of B028, B034 or B046, since the first-round files show a three-way split; I have not verified priority details beyond my own recollection.
statement.conflict_note: No recusal issue for B028 is apparent from my profile; none of its credited names appears among my documented connections. I share a Chalmers affiliation with Olsson, who also prefers B028 with the same trio, and I disclose it as an institutional colleague link, not a stake in the candidates. My Chalmers and WACQT ties are to superconducting-circuit work and to colleagues associated with the 2025 prize, which would matter only if circuit QED (B035) were discussed; it is not on this shortlist. I have no documented connection to Katori, Ye, MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero, Bistritzer or Andrei.
